dedupe_keys.name: edenville and sanford dam failures michigan may 2020 asdso case study and independent forensic report

description: On 19 May 2020, after days of rain, the Edenville and Sanford dams on the Tittabawassee River in central Michigan failed, two of four hydropower dams built in 1923 to 1925 and owned by the same company, with downstream flooding causing extensive property and environmental damage but no deaths. The ASDSO case study records that about 10,000 people were evacuated starting about 18 hours before either dam was sure to fail, saving an estimated 10 to 20 lives, and describes the Edenville embankment, 52 feet high and 6,130 feet long, whose spillway could pass only about 20 to 50 percent of the probable maximum flood, upgrade costs of 5 to 10 million dollars against about 2 million dollars annual revenue, and the 2018 revocation of its licence. The independent forensic team's final report of 4 May 2022 found the likely cause was static liquefaction, that the failures were foreseeable and preventable, and that no single party was to blame. Coverage: four dams in series on one river. Access: free web pages; the licence is not stated. Caveats: the ASDSO pages summarise the forensic reports, and the full report was not read. It supports cascading dam failure, evacuation and ownership-financing analysis, and relates to the Toddbrook spillway failure and ASDSO emergency warning lessons in the catalogue.
